Very long (dozens of hours, at your own pace)

An exploration quest covering the whole Tibia map, tracked on the {wiki:Cyclopedia|Cyclopedia} map. You discover subareas by finding 7 *Points of Interest* in each one, and by completing whole areas you unlock map information, raid warnings and achievements. After 10, 15 and 20 areas, {npc:Charos} gives you the {wiki:Discoverer Outfits|Discoverer Outfits} and the two addons.
There is no minimum level to start, but some subareas are behind level doors (up to 250) and others require access quests (see the areas table).
Several access quests to reach all the zones of the map.
Money for trips all over the map
to go to the Adventurers' Guild to collect the rewards
New information on the Cyclopedia map for each area (NPCs, passages, creatures)
{wiki:Discoverer Outfits|Discoverer Outfits} (10 areas), 1st addon (15 areas) and 2nd addon (20 areas)
Extra information on the Cyclopedia map (NPCs, passages and creatures)
Per area: with **30%** discovered you see the NPC positions; with **70%** the passages to other floors and the teleports; with **100%** the list of creatures in each subarea.
When you discover **100%** of an area: a warning 1 hour before a raid in that area and, 15 minutes before, the exact subarea.
It does not work for underground raids.
You can only discover **one subarea at a time**: if you start another, you lose the progress on the current one.
Start discovering **outside** the subarea: Points of Interest are not generated on the current game screen.
In open areas, sweep the area from **top to bottom** (north–south): the screen is 15x11 squares, so you see more squares per step (over 35% more efficient).
The {wiki:TibiaMaps|TibiaMaps} site (tibiamaps.io/map/poi) already has most of the possible Points of Interest marked on the map.

Tibia is divided into **20 areas**, and each area into several **subareas**. For example, the Thais area has Thais City, Thais Surroundings, Greenshore, Fibula, Mount Sternum, Thais Trolls' Cave, etc.
The quest has two "missions" in the quest log:
The discovery progress of the active subarea
The number of fully discovered areas
2. A Speck of Land: discovering a subarea
Open the {wiki:Cyclopedia|Cyclopedia}, switch to the **Map** tab, click the subarea you want to discover and then the **Start Discovering** button. Confirm your choice.
Do this while you are **outside** the subarea, so that no easy point is excluded for being on your screen.

Several *Points of Interest* are placed randomly in the subarea (different for each player). Walk around the subarea until you find **7**. Once you reach 7, the subarea is unlocked forever on that character and you can start another one.
If you start discovering another subarea before finishing, the progress on the current one is erased.
Follow these rules while you explore:
A message appears at the bottom of the screen whenever you enter or leave the subarea you are discovering. Pay attention so you do not search outside the valid zone.
A subarea can span several floors. City subareas usually include the sewers, the upper floors of public buildings, the walls and the watchtowers.
Points are invisible if you are on another floor. Go up and down even if there seems to be nothing there.
More than 7 points are generated per subarea, but you can get stuck. In that case you can reset the location of the points, but you lose the progress on that subarea.
In large open areas, sweep the area from top to bottom instead of side to side (over 35% more efficient, because the screen is 15x11 squares).

Some squares, such as quest doors or breakable walls, are not part of the subarea: when you walk through them you get the message that you left, even if the area ahead also counts. Always step into the next room to confirm.
Points are chosen randomly from a fixed list. TibiaMaps (tibiamaps.io/map/poi) already includes most of them.
Example: level door of the Medusas and Serpent Spawns dungeon under Talahu
These subareas have particularities worth knowing before you start:
The hall and the stands of each city's {wiki:Duelling Arena|Duelling Arenas} and {wiki:Monster Arena|Monster Arenas} are part of the city's subarea.
The {wiki:Tibian Prize Exhibition|Tibian Prize Exhibition} is part of Thais City. Outside of Sunday it can be hard to find the 7 points and you may have to reset the points.
The exhibition area of the {wiki:Museum of Tibian Arts|Museum of Tibian Arts} counts as Thais Surroundings.

It is advisable to get shipwrecked on {wiki:Arctic Faun's Island|Arctic Faun's Island} (it happens by chance). Otherwise, you may have to reset the points hundreds of times to find them only on the island reached via {wiki:Folda|Folda}. Bind a key to the action "Dialogs: Open Cyclopedia - Map" to reset faster.
It can only be explored when it is open because of the Orc Raid.
The small slope east of Vengoth also counts; you can find a point by climbing the ramp from the Zao Steppe ({coord:33010,31437,7}).

Includes the {wiki:Zao Palace Antechambers|Zao Palace Antechambers} and the {wiki:Zao Palace|Zao Palace}. You can usually find 6 or 7 points without entering the palace, but if you are missing one you may have to face Drakens.

Includes Razachai's Inner Sanctum, the area of the {wiki:Wrath of the Emperor Quest|Wrath of the Emperor Quest}, with {creature:Ghastly Dragon|Ghastly Dragons} and {creature:Undead Dragon|Undead Dragons}.
Ragnir's {creature:Stone Golem|Stone Golems} cave ({coord:32081,31375,8}) is part of Krimhorn (Barbarian Camp).
Points are also generated inside the {wiki:Alawar's Vault Quest|Alawar's Vault Quest} cave. Combine that quest (long route) with exploring Folda: the cave can only be reached with certain keys.
Points can also appear inside boss rooms.
Points may appear in an area whose access is obtained in the last main mission of the {wiki:Shadows of Yalahar Quest|Shadows of Yalahar Quest}.
It has points in {wiki:Deeper Banuta|Deeper Banuta}, which requires the {wiki:The Ape City Quest|The Ape City Quest}.
The entrance area of {wiki:Gray Island|Gray Island} (before the vortex) counts as Edron Surroundings.
As you discover subareas of an area, you gain new features on that area's map:
NPC positions of that area on the map
Passages to subareas on other floors of the map; teleports shown as stairs symbols

List of creatures when you click a subarea's name or a passage symbol (those you do not have in the Bestiary yet appear as a silhouette); a warning 1 hour before a raid in that area and, 15 minutes before, of the exact subarea (except underground raids); the area's achievement and 1 progress point towards the Discoverer Outfits
If a raid in Northern Darama does not show the 15-minute warning with the subarea, it is a raid in Drefia (underground).

Discover all the subareas of each area to receive the corresponding achievement. The numbers in square brackets are the level required by level doors; the asterisk means you can get around the requirement by resetting the points.

When you complete **10 areas** you receive the message: *"Awesome! You have already discovered 10 areas completely! Go and find Charos. He might have a little reward for such an ambitious discoverer like you."*

Go to the {wiki:Adventurers' Guild|Adventurers' Guild}, on an island west of the Thais lighthouse: in the temple of any city, use an {item:Adventurer's Stone} to be teleported there (if you do not have one, ask for another from an NPC in the temple: {key:hi}, {key:adventurer's stone}, {key:yes}). Talk to {npc:Charos}. Say {key:hi}, {key:outfit}, {key:yes}, {key:yes} and then the number of areas you have completed: {key:ten}, {key:fifteen} or {key:twenty}. With 10 areas you receive the outfit and the **Widely Travelled** achievement.

Repeat the conversation with {npc:Charos} when you have **15 areas** (answer {key:fifteen}) for the first addon and **20 areas** (answer {key:twenty}) for the second addon. With the second addon you also earn the **Measuring the World** achievement.

To leave, step on the Guild's teleport: it takes you back to the city you came from. If you prefer to appear in another city, {npc:Charos} can change the teleport's destination ({key:service}).
When you explore **50%** of the map's areas you receive the **Dedicated Entrepreneur** title; when you explore **100%**, the **Globetrotter** title.
